summary: The accepted TE-23 analysis is the local factual core. Repository-level planning research supports dependency-aware decomposition, but it does not establish that one large outer card is universally cheaper than linked small cards.

items.text: TE-23 — Dynamic Workflows as a Task-Cutting Strategy: accepted cost model, decision rubric, capability matrix and limitations.
Agent Studio pipeline-time-economy brief: corpus scope and aggregate coding/review token shares.
Agent Studio pipeline-time-economy analysis: per-step compute, deterministic gate repetition and retry amplification.
Claude Code workflow documentation: scripted runtime, headless behavior, cost guidance and workflow approvals.
Claude Code subagent documentation: subagent configuration and permission modes.
Codex subagent documentation: parallel delegation, custom agent models and non-interactive approval boundary.
Codex non-interactive mode reference: codex exec sandboxing and event output, without a verified subagent lifecycle contract in the supplied analysis.

CodePlan (FSE 2024) evaluates repository-level coding with dependency-aware planning and reports gains over plan-free baselines, supporting explicit cross-file task structure rather than an unbounded single instruction.

SWE-agent (NeurIPS 2024) studies an agent-computer interface for repository issue resolution and shows that action and observation design materially affects outcomes; it supports qualified runtimes, not a particular card size.

Runtime-Structured Task Decomposition (2026 preprint) evaluates adaptive decomposition for software agents; the recency and preprint status require replication before using it as a production threshold.
